LineageEdgeAnswer.description: One way an input influences an output of the job.

input_column.description: For a column edge, the input column; for a parameter edge, the parameter name such as @AsOfDate; else null.
input_column.title: Input Column

input_kind.description: column: a column of one of the job's input tables; parameter: a job parameter such as @AsOfDate; constant: a literal in the code; generated: a value the engine makes, such as an IDENTITY key or a load timestamp.
input_kind.title: Input Kind

input_table.description: For a column edge, the job INPUT table it belongs to, schema-qualified (trace through temp tables and work data sets back to the job's inputs); else null.
input_table.title: Input Table

kind.description: derives: the input's value flows into the output column; filters: it decides which rows appear (WHERE, JOIN ON, HAVING, IN=, subsetting IF); ranks: it decides which row survives (ORDER BY in a ROW_NUMBER, NODUPKEY, FIRST./LAST.).
kind.title: Kind

lines.description: Line numbers in the legacy file that show the edge.
lines.title: Lines

output_column.description: The output column the edge feeds; null for an edge that decides which rows appear (a filter) or which row survives (a ranking).
output_column.title: Output Column

output_table.description: The job's output table, schema-qualified, e.g. rpt.claims_summary.
output_table.title: Output Table

transform.description: A few words on the logic, e.g. 'UPPER(RTRIM(lob_code))'.
transform.title: Transform

structured_output.notes: The payment_date <= &as_of filter (line 36) controls which payments are summed. It does not drop claim rows: every claim on stg.claims appears in the output because of `if c`. first_payment_date and last_payment_date come from the first and last payment in _row_seq (keying) order, not the earliest and latest payment_date. If payments were keyed out of date order, the two can differ from MIN and MAX. For claims with no payments (not p), n_payments, n_recoveries, total_paid and recovery_flag are set to 0. indemnity_amt, expense_amt, recovery_amt and the payment dates are left missing, so gross_paid is missing too (+ on missing values gives missing). net_paid uses sum() and is also missing when all three amounts are missing. Watch for this in the PySpark port. Also, gross_paid is missing for a paid claim whose payments are all one type (for example indemnity only), because the other amount stays 0 there, not missing. In fact both amounts start at 0 for every paid claim, so gross_paid is only missing for claims with no payments. Payment types other than INDEMNITY, EXPENSE and RECOVERY count toward total_paid but toward no split column. n_recoveries and recovery_flag depend on the sign of amount, not on payment_type.
